text:
jordan: FYI nightly eval flagged a weird regression in the sentiment suite for the new bf16-converted candidate. polarity inversion across ~18% of the short summarization prompts. not a latency/cost issue, it's a quality flip.
adele: whoa, 18% is huge. which artifact/version was this?
jordan: rwin-3b-bf16-converted (conversion run #2026) — only difference from baseline is the float16->bf16 conversion step we added yesterday.
matt: can you paste the failing example(s)?
jordan: sure — example 1: prompt "Summarize: The product launched and everyone loved it." baseline: positive summary. candidate: "There were major complaints and disappointment."
kai: that reads like a sign flip in logits for tokens mapping to positive/negative words. any change in tokenizer?
jordan: tokenizer unchanged. conversion script is the only new piece. ci-bot: nightly-eval job #5123 uploaded artifacts and metrics to S3: s3://ci-redwood/nightly/2801239999/metrics.json :eyes:
lina: reproduced locally: running candidate through the sentiment-check harness shows negative probability mass increased for positive-label prompts. distribution plot attached (pasted inline).
matt: can you dump a few intermediate logits before softmax for a failing prompt?
jordan: pasted below (truncated):
```
# baseline logits (pos token cluster): [3.2, 2.9, 3.1]
# candidate logits (same positions): [-1.1, -0.9, -1.0]
```
adele: wow that's a clear sign inversion, not just scale shift.
kai: could be a transpose or sign bug in the conversion that affects QKV or normalization. those can flip signs if weight matrices are permuted incorrectly.
jordan: i pulled the conversion script used: `convert_fp16_to_bf16.py` — suspicious snippet: 
```
# apply grouped transpose for qkv
w = w.reshape(group, -1)
w = w.transpose()
# later
w = w.view(orig_shape)
```
looks too generic. might be reshaping group dims incorrectly.
lina: i grepped the git hash and found one line changed in conversion: `w = w.view(group, -1)` added to support grouped qkv packing. if group ordering is wrong, it would reorder channels.
matt: try reverting the conversion and re-run eval to confirm.
jordan: did that — reverted conversion step, re-eval shows baseline-level metrics (polarity inversion down to 0.3%). confirmed rollback fixes it.
adele: good repro. root cause hypothesis: grouped reshape/transpose in conversion script accidentally permutes q/k/v subblocks for some attention layers, producing sign/position changes in linear projections for tokens that express sentiment.
kai: actionable mitigations: 1) block the current conversion artifact from promotion, 2) add unit test that compares token-level logits (or sign vectors) between baseline and converted for a small curated sentiment promptset, 3) add checksum / shape-contract assertions in conversion script, 4) add canary gating in CI to run this sign-check before allowing deployment.
matt: also add a small layer-wise sanity check: after conversion, compute cosine similarity of per-layer weight matrices to original; if any layer < 0.85 raise alert.
jordan: created a quick patch PR to conversion script with shape assertions + explicit qkv reorder mapping and unit tests: https://git.internal/rwin/convert/pulls/42
lina: i kicked off a gated canary run with the reverted artifact (blocked candidate). canary will include: sentiment-sign-check, structured-output-preservation, and top-k token stability tests.
ci-bot: deploy pipeline: artifact rwin-3b-bf16-converted marked as BLOCKED by gate (test failure: sentiment-sign-check).
adele: next steps: (a) rollback enforced (done), (b) add the new unit tests to nightly and PR gates (jordan + matt), (c) add canary rule to block any conversion artifact until sign-check passes (kai), (d) do a short postmortem doc with exact failing layers and conversion lines (lina).
kai: i'll own the gating change and add the cosine-sim threshold and token-sign-check flags. ETA EOD.
jordan: i'll finish the conversion PR and include a deterministic repro script + minimal failing promptset.
matt: i'll pair-review the PR and add CI job.
lina: i'll draft the postmortem and include mitigation timeline + code pointers.
adele: thanks team. lesson: conversion scripts need strict shape/ordering contracts and lightweight per-token sanity checks before we trust floating-point conversions. :white_check_mark:
jordan: filing a short incident note and linking to this thread. thanks all. :coffee:
ci-bot: nightly-eval job annotated: regression root-cause suspected in conversion script; rollback applied; follow-ups assigned.
